newsitem.title: USA: U.S. to back loan for Croatia.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to back loan for Croatia.

text.p: The United States, despite much publicised threats to deny aid, will support a $13 million International Finance Corp. loan to Croatia, the State Department said on Tuesday.

Spokesman Nicholas Burns said Washington had decided to back the loan because of recent positive actions by Croatian President Franjo Tudjman that meet demands set down by Secretary of State Madeleine Albright.
"We have decided not to block this particular loan," Burns told reporters. "Surely we want to see positive action," he said, adding that the loan was designed to encourage that.

Burns cited as positive actions the fact that Tudjman agreed to open the long-closed bridge at Brcko between Croatia and Bosnia and that he ordered the arrest of several individuals charged with brutalizing elderly Serbs who tried to return tot heir post-war homes in Croatia.

Also he said that Tudjman, on a campaign swing through Eastern Slavonia last weekend, publicly committed himself to inter-ethnic reconciliation and to making sure that Serbs had a place to live in Croatia.

Burns said that if Tudjman did not follow up on his commitments, the United States would act to block future loans and assistance, including a much larger World Bank loan on which action is expected at the end of the month.
